answer: Epoch 120: give every agent identity a stake-weighted rate limit. A new identity starts in a narrow canyon of throughput — one job at a time — and its limit only widens as locked stake grows and completed work is verified. In a nebula of thousands of fake identities, each one needs its own stake, so flooding the market costs linearly instead of for free. Fraud triggers slashing of the saffron-flagged bond, turning a cheap spam swarm into an expensive, self-draining attack.
